rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.4 and 3.1-3.4 report the authors' own sap-flow, microlysimeter and eddy covariance measurements in a super intensive olive orchard (2011-2012), their calibration/validation of SIMDualKc, and their application of METRIC to 16 Landsat 5/7 images, with comparisons of ET and Kc between models and ground data (Tables 3-5, Figs 2-8).
rows.notes: The study's own result is that METRIC (Landsat-based) ET and Kc agree with ground-derived ET and with SIMDualKc (mean bias ~18-20%, Kc correlation R2=0.86). It validates the remote-sensing ET/Kc estimates but does not test or report any water management strategy, irrigation scheduling change, or water saving derived from the satellite products; the use of the information to support improved irrigation management is stated only as a future aim (Introduction, Conclusions). The claim of applicability for fine-tuned water management is therefore a precondition supported (accurate ET/Kc estimation) rather than the claimed effect (water conservation delivered). Also noted: study limitations such as short EC series (n=13/28), few microlysimeter days (n=8), single orchard, one-source SEB limitations for discontinuous canopies, and frost/pruning disturbance in 2012; SD of ETMETRIC across pixels is reported (0.19-0.82 mm/d) - but these do not count because Q2 is no.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is a methodological ET/Kc estimation study (SIMDualKc vs METRIC) in one super intensive olive orchard in Southern Portugal; it validates satellite-based ET estimation but does not evaluate water management outcomes.
